question: What is the primary characteristic of a learning disability regarding a person's intelligence?

options.A: Intelligence is generally average or above average
options.B: Intelligence is below the measurable threshold
options.C: Intelligence is severely and globally impaired

explanation: People with learning disabilities have normal or high intelligence levels, but their brains process specific types of information differently. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h1)

question: How do learning disabilities differ from global developmental delays?

options.A: Learning disabilities impact every single area of daily physical and mental functioning
options.B: Global delays only appear during adulthood while learning disabilities appear in infancy
options.C: Learning disabilities affect specific academic areas while overall intelligence remains intact
options.D: Global delays are caused exclusively by environmental factors rather than brain function

explanation: Specific learning challenges target isolated skills like reading or math, unlike global delays that affect all areas of development. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which learning disability specifically impairs a person's ability to perform mathematical calculations?
explanation: Dyscalculia is the specific neurological term for difficulties involving numbers and math concepts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h2)

question: A student struggles heavily with handwriting, spacing words, and holding a pencil firmly. Which condition fits these signs best?
explanation: Dysgraphia directly interferes with the physical and mental processes of writing and putting thoughts onto paper. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is a major known contributor to the development of learning disabilities?

options.A: Spending too much time playing outdoors
options.B: Eating excessive refined sugar as a toddler
options.C: Lack of strict discipline in the home

explanation: Learning disabilities often run in families, highlighting a strong genetic link in how the brain develops and processes information. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which prenatal event is most associated with an increased risk of neurological learning differences?

options.C: Mild morning sickness during the first trimester
options.D: A pregnant mother eating a high-protein diet

explanation: Perinatal complications like oxygen shortage can disrupt normal brain development, leading to later learning difficulties. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which sign is commonly seen in school-aged children with an undiagnosed learning disability?

options.A: Total loss of voluntary motor movement
options.B: Complete inability to recognize family members
options.C: Sudden blindness occurring only at night
options.D: Persistent reading errors and letter reversals

explanation: School-aged children typically show signs through ongoing struggles with reading, spelling, and academic tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h4)

question: An adult patient consistently struggles with time management, meeting deadlines at work, and organizing written reports despite being very intelligent. What is a likely underlying cause?

options.A: A sudden onset of a degenerative memory disease
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiency causing temporary confusion
options.C: Deliberate refusal to follow workplace guidelines
options.D: Adult manifestations of an unrecognized learning disability

explanation: Adults with learning disabilities often struggle with executive function tasks like organization, time management, and written expression. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of developmental screening tools used by nurses?

options.A: To replace formal psychological testing in schools
options.B: To flag children who need a comprehensive evaluation
options.C: To provide an immediate and final medical diagnosis
options.D: To measure the exact intelligence quotient score

explanation: Screening tools are meant to identify warning signs early so specialists can perform formal, in-depth assessments. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why is listening to parental concerns so critical during a nursing developmental assessment?

options.A: Parents can accurately prescribe educational therapies
options.B: Parents hold medical degrees that speed up diagnosis
options.C: Parents often notice subtle discrepancies in daily functioning first
options.D: Parents are legally required to sign all diagnostic tests

explanation: Caregivers spend the most time observing their children and frequently spot early behavioral or learning red flags before anyone else. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of an assistive technology used for learning disabilities?
explanation: Assistive technologies like text-to-speech programs help individuals bypass reading barriers to access written content. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h6)

question: A nurse is teaching a parent how to help their child complete homework without getting overwhelmed. What strategy is best to recommend?

options.A: Force the child to finish everything in one long session
options.B: Break large assignments into smaller, manageable steps
options.C: Ignore the homework struggles so the child learns independently
options.D: Punish the child whenever a mistake is made on paper

explanation: Breaking tasks down reduces cognitive overload and anxiety for children who struggle with processing large amounts of information. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h6)

question: How can a learning disability affect other children in the family?

options.A: Siblings may experience feelings of neglect or added stress
options.B: Siblings automatically develop the exact same learning disability
options.C: Siblings lose all of their academic abilities
options.D: Siblings are completely unaffected by the situation

explanation: Family dynamics shift when one child requires extensive attention and advocacy, which can impact brothers and sisters emotionally. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the most effective nursing action when supporting stressed parents of a newly diagnosed child?

options.A: Focus only on the child and ignore parental emotional health
options.B: Tell them to stop worrying because children always outgrow it
options.C: Connect them with local parent support groups and active listening
options.D: Advise them to change schools immediately without investigation

explanation: Emotional support and peer connections help parents cope with the challenges of navigating a new diagnosis. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which professionals are typically part of the multidisciplinary team for a child with a learning disability?

options.B: Radiologists, lab technicians, and hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses, educational psychologists, and speech therapists
options.D: Surgeons, pharmacists, and hospital administrators only

explanation: A collaborative team approach involves health and educational specialists working together to support the child's specific needs. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is a key role of the nurse when working with community resources for special needs in Nigeria?

options.A: Diagnosing psychiatric disorders without professional consultation
options.B: Passing strict laws to penalize families who hide children at home
options.C: Connecting families to available local support services and reducing stigma
options.D: Building private special education schools using hospital funds

explanation: Nurses serve as advocates and liaisons, helping families find help in their communities while fighting against societal stigma. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h8)
